source_name: Xuling Hou, Lingxi Li and Tao Wang, “Star edge-coloring of some special graphs”, arXiv:2010.14349 (2020).
statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic graph. The **Dvořák–Mohar–Šámal conjecture.**

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{star}}'(G) \leq 6.
$$

The star chromatic index is the minimum number of colors in a star edge-coloring, in which every bichromatic subgraph contains no path or cycle of length four. The conjecture improves the known upper bound $\chi_{\mathrm{star}}'(G)\leq 7$ for subcubic graphs and remains open.
technical_screen: All finite subcubic graphs, including bridged and cubic graphs, require a six-color star edge-coloring. A local recoloring must forbid bichromatic four-edge paths across every boundary; no invariant achieving this is available. Small examples do not settle the universal bound.

source_name: Jamie Scott, “On the Topological Complexity of Maps”, arXiv:2011.10646 (2020).
statement:
Let $f:G\to H$ be a homomorphism between discrete groups. Let $Bf:BG\to BH$ be a map between Eilenberg–MacLane spaces inducing $f$ on fundamental groups, and let $\beta_H\in H^1(H;I(H))$ be the Berstein–Schwarz class of $H$, where $I(H)\subset\mathbb Z[H]$ is the augmentation ideal. The LS-category of $f$ is defined by $\operatorname{cat}(f)=\operatorname{cat}(Bf)$. **Berstein–Schwarz conjecture.** The LS-category of $f$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{cat}(f)=\max\{k\mid f^*\beta_H^k\neq 0\}.
$$

This conjecture extends the Berstein–Schwarz characterization of the cohomological dimension of a group from the identity map to arbitrary homomorphisms. The supplied text does not state whether the formula is known or unresolved.
technical_screen: Arbitrary discrete group homomorphisms, including unbounded category, are quantified. The easy cup-length lower bound does not supply the categorical upper bound; needs obstruction/cohomological-dimension comparison for maps, not just groups.

source_name: Andrei Benguş-Lasnier, “Minimal Pairs, Truncations and Diskoids”, arXiv:2012.07780 (2021).
statement:
Let $b[?]$ be a valuation and $Q$ an abstract key polynomial (ABKP) for $b[?]$. For an associated diskoid $b[?](Q,b[?](Q))$, let $b[?]_{b[?](Q,b[?](Q))}$ denote the induced function on $b[?][X]$. An **RT extension** is the type of residually transcendental extension considered in the paper. **Diskoid valuation conjectures.** (C1) If $Q$ is an ABKP for $b[?]$, then $b[?]_{b[?](Q,b[?](Q))}$ is a valuation. (C2) If $b[?]$ is an RT extension, then there is a unique diskoid $D$ such that

$$
b[?]=b[?]_D.
$$

These conjectures seek, respectively, multiplicativity of the diskoid-induced function for abstract key polynomials and uniqueness of diskoid representation for RT extensions; the preceding counterexample shows that the analogous assertion does not hold for arbitrary diskoids.
technical_screen: Both C1 and C2 depend on corrupted valuation symbols b[?] and omitted diskoid/RT definitions. Multiplicativity and uniqueness cannot be screened faithfully without primary definitions. No small counterexample asserted.

source_name: Dylan Heuer and Jessica Striker, “Partial permutation and alternating sign matrix polytopes”, arXiv:2012.09901 (2022).
statement: Let $\mathcal{P}(m,n)$ denote the partial permutohedron. **Volume conjecture.** The normalized volume of $\mathcal{P}(m,2)$ is equal to $3^m-m$. This conjecture gives a closed formula for a family of partial permutohedra whose volumes are otherwise difficult to compute; the paper establishes the analogous formula for $\mathcal{P}(2,n)$ but leaves this family as a conjecture.
technical_screen: For every positive integer m, exact target 3^m-m is proved by Behrend et al., arXiv2207.14253v3 Theorem5.11 Eq5.8 pp28-29. Read original2012.09901v1 Definition5.4 and Conjecture5.28 p19, successor Definition2.5 and full Theorem5.11 proof. Removing m disjoint translated unit simplices from 3Delta_m gives the formula. This defeats credit irrespective of registry availability.

source_name: Anders Claesson, “From Hertzsprung's problem to pattern-rewriting systems”, arXiv:2012.15309 (2021).
statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}_k$ be the set of Hertzsprung patterns of length $k$, let $\tau\in\mathcal{S}_k$, and let $|\mathcal{S}_n(\tau)|$ denote the number of length-$n$ objects avoiding $\tau$. Write $\mathrm{id}_k$ for the identity pattern of length $k$. **Bóna's maximal-avoidance conjecture.** For every Hertzsprung pattern $\tau\in\mathcal{S}_k$ and every natural number $n$,

$$
|\mathcal{S}_n(\tau)|\leq |\mathcal{S}_n(\mathrm{id}_k)|.
$$

Bóna proved the inequality for non-self-overlapping patterns. The paper reports computational evidence suggesting that self-overlapping patterns also satisfy it, but gives no general proof.
technical_screen: Quantifies every Hertzsprung pattern of every length and every n, including self-overlap. A single coefficient check cannot establish the avoidance dominance; overlap-cluster signs lack a uniform comparison mechanism.

source_name: John Adamski, Yunchun Hu, Yunping Jiang and Zhe Wang, “Symmetric Rigidity for Circle Endomorphisms with Bounded Geometry”, arXiv:2101.06870 (2021).
statement: Let $f$ and $g$ be uniformly quasisymmetric circle endomorphisms of the same degree $d\geq 2$ with $f(1)=g(1)=1$, and suppose both preserve Lebesgue measure on the circle. Let $h$ be the conjugacy from $f$ to $g$ satisfying $h(1)=1$, so that $h\circ f=g\circ h$. **Symmetric rigidity conjecture.** The conjugacy $h$ is a symmetric circle homeomorphism if and only if $h$ is the identity. This is presented as a more general conjecture than the uniformly symmetric case; the paper cites earlier partial work, but the assertion remains open.
technical_screen: For all Lebesgue-preserving uniformly quasisymmetric maps of a common degree, symmetry of the normalized conjugacy must force identity. No distortion-to-measure uniqueness bridge is supplied; the uniformly symmetric subclass is insufficient.

source_name: Shreejit Bandyopadhyay, “Andrews-Beck Type Congruences Related to the Crank of a Partition”, arXiv:2101.10910 (2021).
statement:
Let $q$ be a formal variable, and define

$$
G(q)=\frac{1}{(q;q^5)_{\infty}(q^4;q^5)_{\infty}},\qquad H(q)=\frac{1}{(q^2;q^5)_{\infty}(q^3;q^5)_{\infty}}.
$$

Here $(a;q)_{\infty}=\prod_{j\geq 0}(1-aq^j)$ denotes the infinite $q$-Pochhammer symbol. **The modulo 5 decomposition conjecture.**

$$
\frac{1}{(q;q)_{\infty}}\sum_{n\geq 1}\frac{(-1)^nq^{\binom{n+1}{2}}(1-q^n)^3(1+q^n)}{1-q^{5n}}=-q(q^{25};q^{25})_{\infty}G(q^5)+q^2(q^{25};q^{25})_{\infty}H(q^5)+q^3(q^{25};q^{25})_{\infty}\frac{H^2(q^5)}{G(q^5)}.
$$

This identity is proposed as part of the decomposition needed to prove the paper's modulo $5$ theorem; the supplied text does not indicate whether it has been resolved.
technical_screen: Exact formal-series identity has Rogers-Ramanujan products and a Lambert-type sum. Coefficient checks would only be instances; need source decomposition and modular-form level/pole bounds before an exact finite certificate could imply the whole identity.

source_name: Orgil-Erdene Erdenebaatar and Uuganbaatar Ninjbat, “The smallest convex K-gon containing N congruent disks”, arXiv:2102.02568 (2021).
statement: Let $n>3$ be a triangular number, and consider the smallest triangle containing $n$ disks and the smallest triangle containing $n-1$ disks. **Erdős–Oler-type conjecture.** The smallest triangle containing $n$ disks is the same as that containing $n-1$ disks. This is presented as a new version of the long-standing Erdős–Oler conjecture. The claim is not established in the source and remains open.
technical_screen: Every triangular n>3 compares two global minimum enclosing triangles for disks. A triangular arrangement yields an upper bound only; no full lower-bound certificate for n-1 disks survives without a packing theorem.

source_name: Philippe Di Francesco, “Twenty Vertex model and domino tilings of the Aztec triangle”, arXiv:2102.02920 (2021).
statement:
For each $n\geq 1$, let $Z^{20V}_n$ denote the total number of 20-vertex configurations with DWBC3 boundary conditions on the quadrangle ${\mathcal Q}_n$, and let $Z^{DT}_n$ denote the total number of $2\times 1$ domino tilings of the Aztec triangle ${\mathcal T}_n$. **Enumeration conjecture.** The two numbers coincide and are given by

$$
Z^{20V}_n=Z^{DT}_n=2^{n(n-1)/2}\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\frac{(4i+2)!}{(n+2i+1)!}.
$$

The formula is presented as conjectural in the concluding discussion and is supported there by numerical data; the supplied paper proves the corresponding identity for the cases $k=1,2,3$, but does not establish this exact product formula in general.
technical_screen: All n enumeration requires precise DWBC3 quadrangle and Aztec triangle definitions. A product determinant or weight-preserving bijection might work, but neither is derived here; reported k<=3 source cases are not a uniform proof.

source_name: Jake Clarkson, Kyle Y. Lin and Kevin D. Glazebrook, “A Classical Search Game in Discrete Locations”, arXiv:2103.09310 (2021).
statement: Let Algorithm~ be the algorithm defined in the paper, let $M$ denote its termination parameter, and let $\epsilon>0$. **Termination conjecture.** Algorithm~ will terminate with $M=\infty$ for any $\epsilon>0$. The conjecture concerns convergence of the algorithm used to compute a minimum expected search cost; the supplied text gives no resolution or further conditions, so its status remains open.
technical_screen: Algorithm identifier is empty and M=infinity is undefined operationally. For each epsilon>0 the actual state transition and termination test must be recovered; no convergence claim possible from this literal row.

source_name: Gregory Gutin and Anders Yeo, “Lower Bounds for Maximum Weighted Cut”, arXiv:2104.05536 (2024).
statement:
Let $G$ be a weighted triangle-free graph, and let $T$ be a spanning tree of $G$. **Spanning-tree bound conjecture.** One should have

$$
\operatorname{mac}(G)\geq \frac{w(G)}{2}+\frac{3w(T)}{8}.
$$

The conjecture would determine the optimal value of the spanning-tree parameter for triangle-free graphs, improving the established lower bound $1/4\leq\theta\leq3/8$ to $\theta=3/8$.
technical_screen: All weighted triangle-free connected instances and every spanning tree require a cut beating half-weight by 3/8 of tree weight. Need primary nonnegative-weight convention and a distribution of cuts with correct correlated tree-edge margins. No such distribution derived.

source_name: Gregory Gutin and Anders Yeo, “Lower Bounds for Maximum Weighted Cut”, arXiv:2104.05536 (2024).
statement:
Let $G$ be a weighted triangle-free graph with maximum degree at most $3$; equivalently, $G$ is a weighted triangle-free subcubic graph. **Weighted subcubic conjecture.** One should have

$$
\operatorname{mac}(G)\geq \frac{4}{5}w(G).
$$

This would extend the known unweighted Bondy–Locke result to edge-weighted graphs. The paper presents the assertion as open.
technical_screen: For every triangle-free subcubic graph and all admissible weights, 4/5-cut bound is a fractional cut-cover statement, stronger than a single unweighted optimum. An unweighted theorem does not automatically lift; no convex combination with each edge cut probability>=4/5 constructed.

source_name: Vahan Mkrtchyan and Garik Petrosyan, “On the fixed-parameter tractability of the partial vertex cover problem with a matching constraint in edge-weighted bipartite graphs”, arXiv:2104.11215 (2021).
statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be the graph in an instance of M-EPVCB, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree. **The degree-deficit hardness conjecture.** M-EPVCB is W[1]-hard with respect to the parameter $|V|-\Delta(G)$. The paper presents this as a suspected strengthening of its discussion of the parameter $\Delta(G)$; no resolution is given in the supplied source.
technical_screen: W[1]-hardness in |V|-Delta requires M-EPVCB definition and a parameter-preserving reduction. No reduction from a canonical hard problem obtained; small graph checking cannot certify hardness.

source_name: Lorenzo Ciardo, “Perron value and moment of rooted trees”, arXiv:2105.03466 (2021).
statement:
Let $T$ be a rooted tree of order $n$, and let $\rho(T)$ denote its Perron value and $\mu(T)$ its moment. **Logarithmic bound conjecture.** There exists $\alpha_0\in\mathbb{R}$ such that

$$
\mu(T)\leq \alpha_0\ln(n)\rho(T)
$$

for every rooted tree $T$ of order $n$. The preceding constructions show that the ratio $\mu(T)/\rho(T)$ is unbounded, while suggesting that its growth is at most logarithmic in the order of the tree.
technical_screen: One constant must control all rooted trees of every n. Need precise moment and rooted Perron matrix; even a logarithmic matrix comparison must be uniform over depth and branching. No full-scope inequality established; n=1 boundary not promoted as a wording correction.

source_name: Cid Reyes-Bustos and Masato Wakayama, “Degeneracy and hidden symmetry – an asymmetric quantum Rabi model with an integer bias”, arXiv:2106.08916 (2021).
statement:
Let $p_{\ell}(x;g,\Delta)$ and $A_N^\ell(u,v)$ be the polynomials defined in the paper, with $g,\Delta$ the coupling and tunnelling parameters. For natural numbers $N,\ell\geq 0$, and for $N\geq\ell$ in the second identity, the conjecture asserts

**Polynomial identity conjecture.** For all natural numbers $N,\ell\geq 0$,

$$
p_{\ell}(N+\tfrac{\ell}{2}-g^2;g,\Delta)=A^\ell_N((2g)^2,\Delta^2),
$$

and, whenever $N\geq\ell$,

$$
p_{\ell}(N-\tfrac{\ell}{2}-g^2;g,\Delta)=A^\ell_{N-\ell}((2g)^2,\Delta^2).
$$

The equality was verified in the paper for $0\leq\ell\leq 6$ and is proposed as a general identity relating the constraint polynomials governing Juddian solutions to the quotient polynomials; its status beyond those checked cases is left open.
technical_screen: Both identities quantify all N,ell and continuous parameters, with N>=ell only in the second. Source recurrence/operator definitions are absent; checking ell<=6 repeats known parameter cases. No all-ell recurrence intertwiner derived.

source_name: Lila Greco and Lionel Levine, “Branching in a Markovian Environment”, arXiv:2106.11249 (2021).
statement:
Let $S$ be the environment state space, let $f(M)=\sum P_nM^n$ be the matrix generating function, and let $E$ be the extinction matrix. Write $I$ for the identity matrix, and let $v$ be the left Perron–Frobenius eigenvector of $E$, normalized so that its coordinates sum to $1$. **Limiting stochastic fixed-point conjecture.** For all environment states $i,j\in S$, 

$$
\lim_{n \to \infty} f^n(I)_{ij} = E_{ij} + \left(1-\sum_{k \in S} E_{ik}\right) v_j.
$$

The conjecture expresses the expected limiting distribution of the environment after $n$ generations on the event of survival. The paper motivates it with experiments; no resolution is supplied.
technical_screen: All states and the n->infinity limit need environment irreducibility/aperiodicity and generating-function conventions. Periodic toy matrices could exploit omitted hypotheses; no source-faithful counterexample or full convergence route asserted.

source_name: Stavros Garoufalidis and Rinat Kashaev, “The descendant colored Jones polynomials”, arXiv:2108.07553 (2022).
statement:
Let $K$ be a knot, let $N$ be a strictly positive integer, let $n$ be an integer parameter, and let $\zeta$ be a primitive $N$-th root of unity. Write $\langle K\rangle_{N,n}$ for the R-matrix invariant, and let $1_N$ denote the identity $N\times N$ matrix. **Matrix-valued colored Jones conjecture.** For all knots $K$, strictly positive integers $N$ and $n$, and primitive $N$-th roots of unity $\zeta$, 
$$
\langle K\rangle_{N,n}=J^K_{n+1}(\zeta)1_N.
$$
 For $n=-1$, the source explains that the invariant is already a multiple of the identity and recovers the specialization entering the Volume Conjecture; the conjecture extends this identity to arbitrary $n\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$.
technical_screen: All knots,N,n and primitive roots require R-matrix normalization and comparison with colored Jones. Matrix scalarity at n=-1 is not the all-n endpoint; no short invariant uniqueness mechanism established.

source_name: Simona Boyadzhiyska, Dennis Clemens, Shagnik Das and Pranshu Gupta, “Ramsey simplicity of random graphs”, arXiv:2109.04140 (2021).
statement: Let $H$ be a bipartite graph. A graph is **$2$-Ramsey simple** when its minimum-degree parameter satisfies $s_2(H)=2(\delta(H)-1)+1$. **Szabó–Zumstein–Zürcher's conjecture.** Every bipartite graph is $2$-Ramsey simple. This conjecture concerns when the general lower bound for the minimum degree of a minimal Ramsey graph is attained; the source gives no evidence here that it has been resolved.
technical_screen: Every bipartite H needs a Ramsey-minimal host with the exact degree 2(delta(H)-1)+1. A sparse arbitrary host or single bipartite family is insufficient; no uniform host construction with certified minimality available.

source_name: Semyon Dyatlov, “Macroscopic limits of chaotic eigenfunctions”, arXiv:2109.09053 (2021).
statement:
Let $(M,g)$ be a compact manifold with Anosov geodesic flow, let $\mu$ be a semiclassical measure on $S^*M$, and let $\mu_L$ denote the Liouville measure. **Liouville-component conjecture.** There exist $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and a probability measure $\mu'$ on $S^*M$ such that

$$
\mu=\alpha\mu_L+(1-\alpha)\mu'.
$$

This conjecture would provide a positive Liouville component for every semiclassical measure and would substantially advance Quantum Unique Ergodicity, although it would not exclude the quantum-cat-map counterexample discussed in the source.
technical_screen: For every Anosov manifold and every semiclassical measure, positive Liouville component is a measure domination assertion. Positive entropy/support alone does not imply it; no bounded exact certificate or full analytic mechanism.

source_name: Ji-Cai Liu and Xue-Ting Jiang, “On the divisibility of sums of even powers of q-binomial coefficients”, arXiv:2110.09906 (2021).
statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $r$ be an arbitrary integer. Write $[n]=(1-q^n)/(1-q)$ for the $q$-integer and let $\Phi_n(q)$ denote the $n$th cyclotomic polynomial. For integers $a$ and $b$, let $\begin{bmatrix}a\\b\end{bmatrix}_q$ denote the $q$-binomial coefficient. **Guo–Schlosser–Zudilin's conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}q^{r(n-k)^2+(r-1)k}\begin{bmatrix}n+k\\k\end{bmatrix}_q^{2r}\begin{bmatrix}n-1\\k\end{bmatrix}_q^{2r}
\equiv q^{(r-1)n+1}[n]-\frac{r(2r-1)(n-1)^2q(1-q)^2}{4}[n]^3\pmod{[n]\Phi_n(q)^3}.
$$

This conjecture unifies earlier conjectures of Gu and Guo and of Guo, Schlosser and Zudilin; the supplied context states that the corresponding congruence modulo $[n]\Phi_n(q)^2$ was still open, and gives no resolution of this stronger modulo $[n]\Phi_n(q)^3$ claim.
technical_screen: All positive n and arbitrary integer r include negative powers of q-binomial factors; primary localization/denominator convention is essential. Root-of-unity expansion might give a route but no denominator-safe uniform expansion to the required fourth-order modulus performed.

source_name: Sarth Chavan, Masato Kobayashi and Jorge Layja, “Integral Evaluation of Odd Euler Sums, Multiple t-Value t(3,2,,2) and Multiple Zeta Value ζ(3,2,,2)”, arXiv:2111.07097 (2021).
statement:
Let $N\in\mathbb{N}$, and write $t(\{2\}^N,1)$ for the multiple $t$-value with $N$ consecutive entries equal to $2$, followed by $1$. Let $I(2N)$ and $\eta(s)$ denote the quantities used in the source. **Identity for $t(\{2\}^N,1)$.** For every $N\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
t(\{2\}^N,1)=\dfrac{I(2N)}{(2N)!}=\dfrac{1}{2^{2N}}\left(\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\dfrac{(-1)^j\pi^{2N-2j}}{(2N-2j)!}\,\eta(2j+1)+(-1)^N2(1-2^{-2N-1})\zeta(2N+1)\right).
$$

The source notes that this multiple $t$-value belongs to the basis predicted by Saha's conjecture, but the displayed assertion is presented as an identity rather than as an unresolved conjecture; its status is therefore unclear from the supplied text.
technical_screen: Every N identity needs definitions of I and eta and convergence convention at N=0. Row itself says displayed identity rather than unresolved conjecture. Primary theorem body required before any novelty claim; no counting an already established evaluation.

source_name: Yair Caro, Mirko Petruševski and Riste Škrekovski, “Remarks on odd colorings of graphs”, arXiv:2201.03608 (2022).
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with maximum degree $\Delta$. **Maximum-degree odd chromatic number conjecture.** If $\Delta\geq3$, then

$$
\chi_o(G)\leq\Delta+1.
$$

This would extend the preceding bounds for subcubic graphs to all connected graphs of maximum degree at least $3$. The statement is presented as a proposed upper bound; its validity is left open in the source.
technical_screen: All connected graphs with Delta>=3 need a proper coloring satisfying odd-neighbor counts. Greedy proper coloring does not preserve the parity witness at all neighbors; no full-scope recoloring invariant.

source_name: Binzhou Xia, Shasha Zheng and Sanming Zhou, “Cubic graphical regular representations of some classical simple groups”, arXiv:2201.08021 (2022).
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite non-abelian simple group. A **cubic GRR** is a graphical regular representation arising from a Cayley graph of valency three.

**Fang–Xia conjecture.** Except for a finite number of cases, every finite non-abelian simple group has a cubic GRR.

The conjecture was proposed after $\mathrm{PSL}_2(7)$ was found to disprove the stronger Fang–Li–Wang–Xu conjecture. The source does not report a resolution of this weaker conjecture.
technical_screen: Cubic GRR for all but finitely many finite nonabelian simple groups requires uniform generation plus automorphism elimination across all families. Individual groups or a known family give no full-scope outcome.

source_name: Nicolas Raymond and Éric Soccorsi, “Magnetic quantum currents in the presence of a Neumann wall”, arXiv:2202.03710 (2022).
statement:
Let $\mu_{1}$ be the first band function, let $\xi_{0}$ denote its minimum point, and write $\mu_{1}^{(3)}(\xi_{0})$ for its third derivative there. **Third-derivative conjecture.**

$$
\mu_{1}^{(3)}(\xi_{0})<0.
$$

This sign condition is supported by numerical simulations and is assumed in part of the subsequent analysis; its general validity is not established in the supplied text.
technical_screen: A rigorous sign certificate for the third derivative at a globally minimizing band parameter needs the actual operator and controlled eigenfunction/resolvent bounds. Numerical evidence alone is inadequate; no interval certificate executed.

source_name: Marija Bliznac Trebješanin, “D(4)-triples with two largest elements in common”, arXiv:2202.04924 (2022).
statement:
Let $\{a_1,b,c\}$ and $\{a_2,b,c\}$ be $D(4)$-triples with

$$
a_1<a_2<b<c.
$$

**Common-largest-elements conjecture.** Then $\{a_1,a_2,b,c\}$ is a $D(4)$-quadruple.

This conjecture asserts a uniqueness-type property for extending $D(4)$-triples with the same two largest elements. The paper states that it is supported by two theorems, but the general assertion remains open.
technical_screen: For all positive ordered D(4)-triples sharing b,c, must force a1*a2+4 square. Finite Pell searches do not bound all b,c; no descent reducing arbitrary solutions to known cases established.

source_name: Maria de Lourdes Merlini Giuliani and Giliard Souza dos Anjos, “Half-isomorphisms of automorphic loops”, arXiv:2203.06230 (2022).
statement:
Let $Q$ and $P$ be automorphic loops, and let $f:Q\to P$ be a half-isomorphism, meaning that for all $x,y\in Q$,

$$
f(x*y)=f(x)*f(y)\quad\text{or}\quad f(x*y)=f(y)*f(x).
$$

**Special half-isomorphism conjecture.** Every half-isomorphism between automorphic loops is special.

The paper proves this assertion for automorphic loops satisfying an additional identity, including automorphic Moufang loops, and notes that known nontrivial examples of half-isomorphisms between automorphic loops are all special. The conjecture proposes that this holds for all automorphic loops.
technical_screen: Special half-isomorphism is not defined in the row. All automorphic loops, including potentially infinite ones, exceed the additional-identity subclass. Need primary definition and a uniform inverse/product consistency argument; no such proof asserted.

source_name: Philip J. Carter, “On the Resolutions of Non-Dicritical Foliations”, arXiv:2203.11094 (2024).
statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a codimension-$1$ foliation, let $V$ range over all truly transversal hypersurfaces, and write $\mathcal{F}|_V$ for the restricted foliation. If $g'=g|_V$ and $b_i'$ are the coordinate functions of the restricted $1$-form, **Transversal restriction conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{ord} g'\leq 1+\operatorname{ord} b_i'
$$

for all $i$ and every truly transversal hypersurface $V$, then the same order relation holds for $\mathcal{F}$. This is presented as a proposed route related to the order criterion for sub-exceptionality; the source does not provide a proof or a counterexample.
technical_screen: The relation for every truly transversal hypersurface must imply the ambient relation. Actual local-ring/order and allowed hypersurface definitions are needed before a generic-slice proof; no automatic routine bridge claimed.

source_name: Damian Sawicki, “Two conjectures on coarse conjugacy by Geller and Misiurewicz”, arXiv:2203.16953 (2024).
statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be unbounded metric spaces, and let $f\colon X\to X$ and $g\colon Y\to Y$ be maps. The maps $f$ and $g$ are **coarsely conjugate** when there are coarse equivalences between $X$ and $Y$ intertwining $f$ and $g$ up to closeness.

**Geller–Misiurewicz's conjecture.** If $f$ and $g$ are coarsely conjugate, then $f^n$ and $g^n$ are coarsely conjugate for every natural number $n$.

The conjecture generalizes the result that powers preserve coarse conjugacy when one of the maps is controlled. The paper proves that the conjecture is false, including examples with identity conjugating maps and, in one construction, invertible dynamics; consequently its status is refuted.
technical_screen: Literal row explicitly reports counterexamples to preservation under all iterates, even with identity conjugating maps and invertible dynamics. No new credit sought; source body not independently audited, so this is a reported resolution rather than certified proof clearance.

source_name: Mortaza Bayat and Hossein Teimoori Faal, “A Generalization of Tepper's Identity”, arXiv:2205.04237 (2022).
statement:
Let $l$ be a positive integer, and let $P(x)$ be a real polynomial of degree $n$ with leading coefficient $a_n$. **Scaled generalized Tepper identity.** One has

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{n}(-1)^k {n \choose k}P(x-lk)=a_n l^n n!.
$$

The preceding theorem proves the case $l=1$ for arbitrary real polynomials. The displayed statement is presented as a conjectural generalization; the supplied text gives no resolution evidence for the scaled case.
technical_screen: For every degree-n real P, all positive l and all x: put Q(t)=P(lt), degree n with leading coefficient a_n*l^n, in source Theorem4.3 at t=x/l. Gives source Conjecture4.5 exactly. Actual arXiv2205.04237v1 pp7-8 theorem/proof and conjecture read. No discovery credit for this classical adaptation.

source_name: Karen Meagher and Andriaherimanana Sarobidy Razafimahatratra, “On the intersection density of the Kneser Graph K(n,3)”, arXiv:2205.05118 (2023).
statement: Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $\operatorname{PSL}_2(q)$ act on the $3$-sets of its natural degree-$q+1$ action. **Intersection-density conjecture.** If $q^2\equiv 1\pmod{5}$, then the intersection density is $4/3$; if $q^2\equiv 4\pmod{5}$, then the intersection density is $1$. These values would determine the intersection density in the two stated congruence cases.
technical_screen: All prime powers in two q^2 mod5 classes require maximum intersecting-family sizes for PSL2 action on triples. Spectral character calculations and matching constructions not supplied; a small-q enumeration would only be a parameter instance.

source_name: Thomas Blomme, “Tropical curves in abelian surfaces III: pearl diagrams and multiple cover formulas”, arXiv:2205.07684 (2024).
statement:
Let $C$ be a curve class, let $g_0$ be fixed, and define the generating series

$$
\mathcal{R}_{g_0,C}=\sum_{g\geqslant g_0}\langle \lambda_{g-g_0};\mathrm{pt}^{g_0}\rangle_{g,C}u^{2g-2}.
$$

Let $R_{g_0,C}(q)$ denote the corresponding refined tropical generating series, and set $q=e^{iu}$. **Generating-series correspondence conjecture.** Through the change of variable $q=e^{iu}$, one has

$$
\mathcal{R}_{g_0,C}=(-1)^{g_0-1}R_{g_0,C}(q).
$$

This is proposed as a generalization to abelian surfaces of a correspondence result relating refined tropical invariants to Gromov–Witten invariants with lambda-class insertions. The source notes that the identity is known for primitive curve classes and for arbitrary curve classes when $g_0=2$.
technical_screen: All curve classes and genera above g0 require refined tropical/GW comparison beyond primitive classes and g0=2. No finite certificate implies all descendant insertions; substantial degeneration machinery missing.

source_name: Saikat Panja and Sachchidanand Prasad, “Counterexample to a conjecture about dihedral quandle”, arXiv:2205.15024 (2022).
statement:
Let $\mathbb{R}_n=\{a_0,a_1,\cdots,a_{n-1}\}$ denote the dihedral quandle of order $n$, and let $\Delta^k(\mathbb{R}_n)$ denote the $k$th power of its augmentation ideal. **Bardakov–Passi–Singh conjecture.** The following statements should hold:

1. For an odd integer $n>1$,
 
$$
\Delta^{k}(\mathbb{R}_{n})/\Delta^{k+1}(\mathbb{R}_{n})\cong \mathbb{Z}_n
$$

 for all $k\ge 1$.
2. For an even integer $n>2$,
 
$$
\left|\Delta^{k}(\mathbb{R}_{n})/\Delta^{k+1}(\mathbb{R}_{n})\right|=n
$$

 for $k\ge 2$.

The first assertion has been confirmed, and the second is known for $n=4$. The paper gives a counterexample showing that the conjecture is false in general, so the combined conjecture is refuted.
technical_screen: Combined odd/all-k and even/k>=2 assertion already reported refuted by source. Confirmed odd part and n=4 even part are known instances, not new outcomes. No independent proof-body audit performed.

source_name: Filippo Beretta, Jesse Dimino, Weike Fang, Thomas C. Martinez, Steven J. Miller and Daniel Stoll, “On Benford's Law and the Coefficients of the Riemann Mapping Function for the Exterior of the Mandelbrot Set”, arXiv:2206.04112 (2023).
statement:
Let $m=2^n m_0$, where $m_0$ is odd, and let $
u=
u_2$ denote the 2-adic valuation. Let $a_m$ be the Taylor coefficients of the reciprocal Riemann mapping function. **Zagier-type conjecture.** For the $a_m$ coefficients, if $n=0$, then

$$
-
u(a_m)=
u((2m-2)!);
$$

if $n=1$, then

$$
-
u(a_m)=
u(((2m-2)/3)!)+\epsilon(m_0),
$$

where $\epsilon(m_0)=1$ if $m_0\not\equiv3\pmod{12}$, while otherwise it follows the pattern in the cited table. This extends the conjectured valuation patterns for the Laurent coefficients $b_m$ to the Taylor coefficients $a_m$. The $n=0$ identity agrees with the known equality case for odd $m$; the $n=1$ pattern, including its exceptional values, remains conjectural.
technical_screen: Even the n=1 assertion refers to an unspecified exceptional epsilon table and factorial((2m-2)/3) without domain convention. Need actual coefficient definition and table; cannot certify full scope or use wording defects for credit.

source_name: Maohua Le, Reese Scott and Robert Styer, “On a conjecture concerning the number of solutions to a^x+b^y=c^z”, arXiv:2206.14032 (2022).
statement:
Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be distinct primes with $a<b$, and let $N(a,b,c)$ denote the number of solutions $(x,y,z)\in\mathbb{N}^3$ to

$$
a^x+b^y=c^z.
$$

**Scott–Styer's prime-base conjecture.** We have $N(a,b,c)\leq1$, apart from the six explicitly listed exceptional cases: $(2,3,5)$, $(2,3,11)$, $(2,5,3)$, $(2,7,3)$, $(3,5,2)$, and $(3,13,2)$, with the solution tuples given in the source statement. This restricted form is used in the paper because the prime-base setting makes the classification problem more tractable; the preceding theorems give substantial restrictions on any non-exceptional counterexample, but the conjecture itself remains open.
technical_screen: All triples of distinct primes except six fixed exceptions and all positive exponents require a global uniqueness theorem. Bounded searches or additional restrictions from source are not full-scope; no new descent route.

source_name: Davide Lombardo and Matteo Verzobio, “On the local-global principle for isogenies of abelian surfaces”, arXiv:2206.15240 (2024).
statement: Let $K$ be a number field, let $\ell$ be a prime, and let $(A,\ell)$ be a **strong counterexample** to the local-global principle for isogenies of prime degree between abelian surfaces, meaning that $A$ has a locally everywhere isogeny of degree $\ell$ but no global one. **Large-prime strong-counterexample conjecture.** There is a constant $b=b(K)$ such that, for all primes $\ell>b(K)$ and all such strong counterexamples $(A,\ell)$, the abelian surface $A$ is geometrically isogenous to the square of an elliptic curve with complex multiplication. This predicts that sufficiently large-prime strong counterexamples can occur only in the CM-square case, after the paper excludes the other relevant monodromy cases for all but finitely many primes.
technical_screen: For each number field K one bound b(K) must work for all large primes and all strong abelian-surface counterexamples. Needs monodromy classification and uniform isogeny restrictions; no short certificate or uniform route.

source_name: Robert Davis and Florian Kohl, “Perfectly Matchable Set Polynomials and h^*-polynomials for Stable Set Polytopes of Complements of Graphs”, arXiv:2207.14759 (2022).
statement:
Let $C_n$ be the cycle graph on $n$ vertices, let $p(C_n;z)$ denote its perfectly matchable set polynomial, and let $\overline{h}^*(C_n;z)$ denote the normalized $h^*$-polynomial of the stable set polytope of the complement of $C_n$. **Cycle polynomial conjecture.** For all $n\geq 4$, 

$$
\overline{h}^*(C_n; z) = p(C_n; z) + \frac{1+(-1)^{n+1}}{2}z^{(n+1)/2}.
$$

The formula agrees with the explicitly computed even-cycle case and with the listed examples through $n=9$; the asserted general identity, particularly for odd cycles, remains open in the source.
technical_screen: For every n>=4 polynomial identity needs normalized h-star and complement-stable-set conventions. Even n known; odd family might admit transfer matrices, but no lattice-point recurrence equated to matchable sets. No instance-only proposal.

source_name: Alexander Perepechko and Mikhail Zaidenberg, “Automorphism groups of rigid affine surfaces: the identity component”, arXiv:2208.09738 (2025).
statement: Let $\mathbb K$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let $Y$ be an affine algebraic variety. Call $Y$ **rigid** if it admits no effective $\mathbb G_{\rm a}$-action, equivalently if $\operatorname{Aut}^{0}(Y)$ contains no $\mathbb G_{\rm a}$-subgroup. **Rigidity conjecture.** If $Y$ is rigid, then $\operatorname{Aut}^{0}(Y)$ is an algebraic torus of rank at most $\dim Y$. The conjecture predicts that the identity component of the automorphism group of a rigid affine variety is algebraic and has the expected dimension bound; the paper's abstract states this as the phenomenon established for affine surfaces, while the displayed conjecture concerns arbitrary affine varieties.
technical_screen: All rigid affine varieties in characteristic zero require proving identity automorphism component is finite-dimensional algebraic and then toric of bounded rank. Surface case does not settle arbitrary dimension; no general algebraicity mechanism.

source_name: Keagan G. Callis, “Absolutely Periodic Billiard Orbits of Arbitrarily High Order”, arXiv:2209.11721 (2022).
statement:
Let $f$ be the billiard map, and call a $q$-periodic orbit **absolutely periodic** when the differential of $f^q$ is the identity and all second-order and higher partial derivatives of $f^q$ vanish at every point of the orbit. **Safarov–Vassiliev's conjecture.** There are no absolutely periodic orbits for Euclidean billiards.

The paper studies absolutely periodic orbits and proves that, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, domains containing absolutely periodic orbits of order $n$ are dense among bounded strictly convex domains with smooth boundary. Thus the conjecture remains open as stated, while the result provides evidence toward its eventual disproof.
technical_screen: Absence of absolutely periodic Euclidean billiard orbits requires every derivative order simultaneously. Density of domains with finite-order flat returns does not imply an infinitely flat example or prohibit one; no compactness argument established.

source_name: Maria Axenovich and Felix Christian Clemen, “Rainbow Subgraphs in Edge-colored Complete Graphs – Answering two Questions by Erdős and Tuza”, arXiv:2209.13867 (2022).
statement:
Let $S(N)$ be the set of natural numbers $q$ such that $4\leq q\leq N$ and, for every $n_0$, there is some $n\geq n_0$ with $n\equiv 1\pmod{\ell}$ and a balanced coloring of $K_n$ in $\binom{q}{2}$ colors containing no rainbow copy of $K_q$. **Clique counterexample conjecture.** For every natural number $N$,

$$
S(N)=\{n\in\mathbb{N}:n\geq 4\}.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the Erdős–Tuza question has a negative answer for every clique of size at least four. The paper proves that $|S(N)|=N-(1+o(1))N/\log N$, showing that most clique sizes have the required counterexamples, while the full assertion remains open.
technical_screen: Literal S(N) is a subset of finite [4,N] yet equated to all integers>=4. This is a truncation/wording inconsistency, not an eligible mathematical refutation. Intended all-clique-size statement still requires new balanced coloring mechanisms and undefined ell convention.

source_name: Liam Armstrong, Bryan Ducasse, Thomas Meyer and Holly Swisher, “Generalized Alder-Type Partition Inequalities”, arXiv:2210.04070 (2022).
statement:
Let $p(n\mid\text{condition})$ count partitions of $n$ satisfying the specified condition. Define

$$
q_d^{(1)}(n):=p(n\mid\text{parts}\geq 1\text{ and differ by at least }d)
$$

and

$$
Q_d^{(1,-)}(n):=p(n\mid\text{parts}\equiv\pm1\pmod{d+3},\text{ excluding the part }d+2).
$$

**Inagaki–Tamura shift identity conjecture.** If $d\geq 12$ and $n\geq d+2$, then

$$
q_d^{(1)}(n)-Q_{d-4}^{(1,-)}(n)\geq 0.
$$

Shift identities of this type can yield information about the modified Alder-type inequalities and improve the bounds in the generalized conjecture. The source gives no resolution of this particular shift identity conjecture.
technical_screen: Every d>=12 and n>=d+2 needs a uniform partition injection or exact coefficient positivity argument. Finite generating-series checks cannot handle all n,d; no admissible injection surviving the shifted exclusion derived.

source_name: Peter Kagey, “Spinning switches on a wreath product”, arXiv:2210.09408 (2022).
statement: Let $G\wr H$ be a wreath product, and call a surjective strategy **palindromic** when its sequence of moves $S'=\{k'_i\in K\}_{i=1}^N$ satisfies $k'_i=k'_{N-i+1}$ for every $i$. **Palindromic strategy conjecture.** Whenever $G\wr H$ has a surjective strategy, it also has a palindromic surjective strategy. The conjecture is motivated by the fact that all examples known to the authors admit such a strategy; the source notes that a counterexample might occur for a trivial wreath product.
technical_screen: For every wreath product admitting a surjective strategy need precise horizon, adversary and prefix/visitation definitions. Appending a reverse move list is only a tempting shortcut; it may violate the source definition and is not claimed as proof.

source_name: Yacine Chitour, Sébastien Fueyo, Guilherme Mazanti and Mario Sigalotti, “Hautus–Yamamoto criteria for approximate and exact controllability of linear difference delay equations”, arXiv:2210.13590 (2025).
statement:
Let $\Lambda_N>0$, $d\in\mathbb{N}$, $q\in[1,+\infty)$, and consider the linear difference delay system with delay parameters and matrices $A_N$ and $B$ described above. Let $H(\mathbb{C})$ denote the corresponding matrix-valued characteristic function, and let $\overline{H(\mathbb{C})}$ be its closure. **Hautus sufficiency conjecture.** The system is $L^q$ exactly controllable in time $d\Lambda_N$ if and only if

$$
\operatorname{rank}[M,B]=d\quad\text{for every }M\in\overline{H(\mathbb{C})},
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{rank}[A_N,B]=d.
$$

The corresponding rank conditions are known to be necessary, while sufficiency would resolve the associated Bézout identity over a Radon measure algebra; this remains an open problem.
technical_screen: All delays/matrices and q in [1,infinity) need exact controllability at fixed time dLambda_N. Necessary rank tests do not produce a Bezout inverse over Radon measures; no finite-dimensional rank computation closes this functional-analytic gap.

source_name: Tao Gui, “Conjectures on the reduced Kronecker coefficients”, arXiv:2210.14668 (2026).
statement:
For partitions $\lambda,\mu,\nu$, let $\bar g_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}$ denote the reduced (or stable) Kronecker coefficient. The saturation property concerns simultaneous scaling of the three partitions.

**Kirillov–Klyachko conjecture.** The reduced Kronecker coefficients satisfy

$$
\bar g_{k\lambda,k\mu}^{k\nu}\ne0\text{ for some }k\geq1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\bar g_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}\ne0.
$$

This conjecture was refuted in general: for every $k\geq3$, $(1^{k^2-1},1^{k^2-1},k^{k-1})$ is a counterexample. Thus the proposed saturation property fails, although special cases may remain valid.
technical_screen: Literal statement already supplies the public counterexample family to reduced-Kronecker saturation for every k>=3. Reproducing a family member is no new discovery. Full source proof not audited in this lane.

source_name: Igor Grzelec and Mariusz Woźniak, “Local Irregularity Conjecture for 2-multigraphs versus cacti”, arXiv:2211.08270 (2022).
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, let $\mathfrak{T'}$ be the family consisting of the recursively defined family $\mathfrak{T}$ together with all odd-length paths and odd-length cycles, and let $B$ be the bow-tie graph. Let ${\rm lir}(G)$ denote the locally irregular chromatic index of a locally irregular colorable graph $G$. **Bow-tie version of the Local Irregularity Conjecture.** Every connected graph $G\notin\mathfrak{T'}$, except for the bow-tie graph $B$, satisfies 
$$
{\rm lir}(G)\leq 3.
$$
 This formulation incorporates the bow-tie counterexample to the original conjecture. The cited work proves the bound for every locally irregular colorable cactus other than $B$, but the general assertion remains unresolved in the supplied text.
technical_screen: All connected graphs outside T-prime and bow-tie require locally irregular three-edge-coloring. Known cactus cases do not extend to general blocks. Related to already-investigated local-irregularity family; no new uniform decomposition, no variant credit.

source_name: Vladimir Shein, “Automorphisms of symmetric powers and motivic zeta functions”, arXiv:2211.13304 (2022).
statement:
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be an $\alpha$-twisted locally free sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}K$ of rank $n$, and let $\mathbb{P}\mathcal{E}$ denote its associated twisted projective space. **The expected class identity.** For every $k\geq 0$, one should have

$$
[\operatorname{Sym}^{nk+1}(\mathbb{P}\mathcal{E})]=[\operatorname{Gr}^{nk+1}(\mathcal{E}^{\oplus(k+1)})].
$$

This is presented as a natural expectation extending the class equality between symmetric powers of projective space and Grassmannians. The source gives no evidence that it has been proved or disproved.
technical_screen: For all k>=0 and twisted rank-n spaces, symmetric-power and Grassmannian classes must agree in the source ring. Birational equivalence alone does not imply Grothendieck-class equality; no stratification respecting the Brauer twist constructed.

source_name: H. Teimoori and H. Khodakarami, “Pascal Determinantal Arrays and a Generalization of Rahimpour's Determinantal Identity”, arXiv:2301.12481 (2026).
statement:
Let $P=(P_{i,j})_{i,j\geq 0}$ be the Pascal infinite array, where

$$
P_{i,j}=\binom{i+j}{i}.
$$

For $k\geq 1$, let $P^{(k)}_{i,j}$ denote the determinant of the $k\times k$ sub-array of $P$ beginning at position $(i,j)$:

$$
P^{(k)}_{i,j}=\det\bigl(P_{i+r,j+s}\bigr)_{0\leq r,s<k}.
$$

**Rahimpour's determinantal identity.** The determinant of the $n\times n$ square sub-array in the Pascal array whose left edge lies in the $k$-th column equals the determinant of the top-right $k\times k$ square sub-array; more precisely,

$$
P^{(k)}_{i,j}=P^{(j)}_{i,k},\qquad i,j\geq 0,\quad k\geq 1.
$$

The case $k=1$ is the previously known Rahimpour identity, while the displayed generalization concerns arbitrary $k\geq 1$ and is presented as a conjecture in the source.
technical_screen: Actual arXiv2301.12481v1 Section2 Conjecture2 Eq2 is explicitly proved by the same paper in final Section proof pp14-16, using double-stick cancellation after determinantal-array identities. Read literal statement, source intent and complete terminal proof. No independent dependency audit of condensation/geometric lemmas, but public exact proof defeats eligibility.

source_name: Martin Winter, “Rigidity, Tensegrity and Reconstruction of Polytopes under Metric Constraints”, arXiv:2302.14194 (2024).
statement: A centrally symmetric polytope is uniquely determined, up to isometry, by its edge-graph, edge lengths, and vertex-origin distances. **Central symmetry reconstruction conjecture.** The stated metric data determine the centrally symmetric polytope up to isometry. This is explicitly described as the centrally symmetric version of the main reconstruction conjecture; the source gives no resolution.
technical_screen: For all centrally symmetric polytopes in all dimensions, graph+edge lengths+vertex radii must determine congruence. A local rigidity matrix or planar case does not establish global reconstruction; no exact flexible pair or global Gram completion theorem derived.

source_name: Maria Axenovich, António Girão, Lawrence Hollom, Julien Portier, Emil Powierski, Michael Savery, Youri Tamitegama and Leo Versteegen, “A note on interval colourings of graphs”, arXiv:2303.04782 (2023).
statement:
Let $\theta(n)$ be the maximum interval colouring thickness of a graph on $n$ vertices. **Subpolynomial thickness conjecture.**

$$
\theta(n)=n^{o(1)}.
$$
 The paper has bounds $\theta(n)=\Omega(\log(n)/\log\log(n))$ and $\theta(n)\leqslant n^{5/6+o(1)}$, so this conjecture remains open.
technical_screen: n^{o(1)} requires for every epsilon>0 eventually thickness<=n^epsilon for all n-vertex graphs. The supplied polynomial upper bound cannot be iterated without a new decomposition; no constructive subpolynomial scheme.

source_name: Benjamin A. Burton and Alexander He, “Finding large counterexamples by selectively exploring the Pachner graph”, arXiv:2303.06321 (2024).
statement:
A **one-vertex triangulation** of a lens space is a triangulation with exactly one vertex, and a **core edge** is an edge that realizes a core curve, whose complement after removing a regular neighbourhood is a solid torus.

**Infinite core-edge counterexample conjecture.** Every lens space admits infinitely many one-vertex triangulations with no core edges.

The paper proves this for six lens spaces, including the 3-sphere, and reports failed searches for many others. It nevertheless conjectures the statement for every lens space; the supplied text gives no resolution.
technical_screen: Every lens space needs infinitely many distinct one-vertex no-core-edge triangulations. Six examples and local moves do not prove a universal seed or preservation of non-core status; no full-scope move invariant established.
